name: בַּעַל בְּרִית
summary: The Baal whom Israel made their god after Gideon died, forgetting Yahweh who had delivered them (Jdg 8:33–34). His house at Shechem gave Abimelech seventy pieces of silver to hire worthless men, with which he killed his brothers (Jdg 9:4–5), and the men of the tower of Shechem fled into the stronghold of the house of אֵל בְּרִית, “god of covenant”, the same god, where Abimelech burned them (Jdg 9:46–49). The name is בַּעַל “owner, lord” with בְּרִית “covenant”: a Baal of covenant, set up at Shechem, where Joshua had cut Israel's covenant with Yahweh (Jos 24:25).

evidence.note: “The sons of Israel went whoring after the Baals and made בַּעַל בְּרִית their god.”
“They did not remember Yahweh their God, who had delivered them.”
Seventy pieces of silver “from the house of בַּעַל בְּרִית”.
“The stronghold of the house of אֵל בְּרִית”: the same god under El.
“Joshua cut a covenant with the people that day … in Shechem.”

note: A god, TIPNR's Supernatural record Baal-berith@Jdg.8.33, which takes both בַּעַל בְּרִית and אֵל בְּרִית. No bdb key: its tokens are בְּרִית (b.da.ab, the root entry's word) with בַּעַל and אֵל, and a key belongs to one entry only. Filed under ברה for the distinguishing element; בעל and אלה have their own entries or will. Whether “of covenant” means a god sworn by in a covenant, or a covenant-god set against Yahweh's covenant at Shechem, scripture does not say.
